title: The Fragile Lock: Novel Bypasses For SAML Authentication
summary: This post details new methods for bypassing SAML authentication in Ruby and PHP environments. The vulnerabilities are found at the parser level, specifically exploiting issues with attribute pollution and namespaces.

title: Cookie Chaos: How to bypass __Host and __Secure cookie prefixes
summary: This post discusses how to bypass cookie defenses, specifically focusing on the __Host and __Secure cookie prefixes. It explains that these prefixes were added by browsers to enhance session protection and prevent malicious cookie setting. The bypass method involves exploiting discrepancies between browser and server implementations.
bullets: Targets prevention of malicious cookie setting

title: Inline Style Exfiltration: leaking data with chained CSS conditionals
summary: This item describes a newly discovered method for data exfiltration using chained CSS conditional logic. The technique allows for the theft of attribute data directly through style attributes, bypassing traditional selector and stylesheet import restrictions.

Leads data using chained CSS conditionals.
Exploits CSS injection via style attributes.

HTTP keep-alive can be mistaken for smuggling

title: HTTP/1.1 must die: the desync endgame
summary: HTTP/1.1 is fundamentally insecure and has led to widespread website takeovers. Despite attempts at mitigation over the past six years, the problem remains unfixed.

title: Repeater Strike: manual testing, amplified

bullets: New Burp Suite extension: Repeater Strike

title: A 0-click exploit chain for the Pixel 10: When a Door Closes, a Window Opens
summary: Researchers developed a two-exploit chain to achieve root access on Google Pixel 10 devices, building on a previous Pixel 9 exploit. They adapted a zero-click vulnerability (Dolby) for the Pixel 10, encountering a challenge with Pixel 10's use of RET PAC instead of -fstack-protector. The team successfully bypassed this by overwriting initialization code (dap_cpdp_init).
bullets: Worked around Pixel 10's RET PAC security.
Used initialization code overwrite for exploit.

title: On the Effectiveness of Mutational Grammar Fuzzing
summary: This post discusses mutational grammar fuzzing, a technique that mutates samples while maintaining their structure based on a predefined grammar. While effective for finding complex bugs, the author identifies flaws in this approach and proposes a simple technique to overcome them.
bullets: Mutational grammar fuzzing maintains sample structure via grammar rules.
Coverage-guided variant saves new coverage-triggering samples.
Technique proven effective for finding complex issues (e.g., browser/JIT bugs).
Post will detail perceived flaws in the approach.
A simple counter-technique will also be presented.

title: A Deep Dive into the GetProcessHandleFromHwnd API
summary: This post examines the GetProcessHandleFromHwnd API, which was discovered through a UAC bypass vulnerability. The API uses a window hook to inject code into a target process and retrieve its handle, but only succeeds if the caller and target processes run as the same user.
bullets: Discovered via Quick Assist UAC bypass
Uses window hook for code injection
Requires same user for both processes

title: Bypassing Administrator Protection by Abusing UI Access

title: Bypassing Windows Administrator Protection

It details research into the feature, including the discovery and patching of nine vulnerabilities that allowed for bypassing Administrator Protection to gain silent administrator privileges. The feature has since been disabled by Microsoft due to an application compatibility issue.

Research uncovered 9 vulnerabilities to bypass the feature.
All reported vulnerabilities have been fixed by Microsoft.
